clue.text: Funny conjuror grabs microphone before a show

indicators.note: the conjuror grabs, so holds, the microphone inside his name

parts.note: Tommy Cooper was a British comedian whose magic act famously went wrong on purpose
mic is the short form of microphone

explanation.surface: A comic magician seizes the mike before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a much-loved British comedy magician in a fez whose tricks went wrong on purpose, hence 'Funny conjuror'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light operatic work with spoken dialogue and a happy ending is a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Fellow from class, one pursued by females

parts.note: cl. is the dictionary abbreviation for class
one is the Roman numeral I
f is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A lad from the form is chased by the girls.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a man, and this is a man's given name.

clue.text: Thin fog over central Urals and wind in part of Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over, so above, the next

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of Urals, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: Light fog lies over the Ural mountains while wind blows across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes RAL from the middle of URALS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cold northerly wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Fancy decoration, including rare carpet: protective cover needed

indicators.note: the reworked letters take in, so contain, the other pieces
fancy as a verb or adjective suggests elaborate rearrangement, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: An ornate decoration incorporating an unusual carpet needs something to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges the letters of decoration; 'including' means that result takes in the rare carpet's letters near its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged galvanised sheeting is used as roofing and shelter, a sturdy covering for sheds and huts.

clue.text: Having wall covering on both sides, bedroom's ultimately spoilt

indicators.note: the papered word sits on either side of, so surrounds, the single letter

parts.note: a room with wallpaper on its walls has been papered

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of bedroom

explanation.surface: A bedroom freshly wallpapered on both walls has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes M, the last letter of bedroom, and 'on both sides' wraps PAPERED around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who is spoilt has been indulged and coddled.

clue.text: Celebrity currently appearing in shortened version of Rent

indicators.note: the word for currently appears inside the shortened word
shortened means the musical's title loses its final letter

parts.note: currently means now, at present

explanation.surface: A star is now appearing in a cut-down production of the musical Rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is a stage musical, so the surface reads as a celebrity in a cut-down production; 'shortened version of' drops its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame: widespread acclaim and repute.

clue.text: Vocally support member of House of Lords

indicators.note: vocally means the word is spoken, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: Someone loudly backs a member of the upper house.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord, a member of the nobility, has a seat in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Abstract of unfinished great work

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: epic means great, heroic in scale
a tome is a large book, a written work

explanation.surface: A summary of an incomplete masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a summary or condensed embodiment, which is what an epitome is.

clue.text: Foreign money financial backer's invested in countryside area

indicators.note: invested here means placed inside, the backer being put into the money

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Overseas funds from an investor go into a rural region.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang an angel is a backer who funds a show; 'invested' plays on money being invested.
explanation.definitionFit: Open land used for grazing livestock is a stretch of countryside.

clue.text: Winter's starting, presumably, and group of directors takes the plunge unintentionally

parts.note: when winter starts, autumn (US fall) is presumably finished: fall's over
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: As winter begins, the board makes a bold decision without meaning to.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn, so 'Winter's starting, presumably' reads as FALL'S OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple off a ship into the sea is to go into the water by accident.

clue.text: Notts team in ruin-poor scoring

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nottinghamshire's side are in ruins after a poor run of scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county. 'poor' rearranges NOTTS TEAM IN RUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring is arranging music for an ensemble of instruments, the orchestration.

clue.text: He appears in satirical programmes a lot

definitions.meaning: John, of the Channel 4 satire team Bremner, Bird and his own surname
a lot of money, a great deal of wealth

explanation.definitionFit: A British satirist shares his surname with the word for a large sum of money or luck.

clue.text: Statute rejected by European prime minister

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a statute is a law
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: A law is thrown out by a European premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert, the Whig leader, is regarded as Britain's first prime minister.

clue.text: One steals large amount, mostly beer

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a pile is a large amount
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone nicks a heap, chiefly of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunderer is someone who steals, looting by force.

clue.text: Hearty supporter for runner in race

definitions.meaning: a device implanted to keep the heart beating regularly
an athlete who sets the speed for others in a race

explanation.definitionFit: A medical device that regulates heartbeat, and a runner who sets the speed, share one name.

clue.text: Chap takes a long time, going round wine store

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap

indicators.note: going round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A fellow dawdles as he walks round the wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Bod is informal British for a person; 'going round' turns the long time back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain a wine cellar or wine shop goes by this name.

clue.text: Noble Italian advances east

parts.note: an army marches when it advances

explanation.surface: An Italian aristocrat strides eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian marquis holds a title of nobility.

clue.text: Sport hit when pound's dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the letter for the pound is taken out

parts.note: to clobber is to hit hard
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A game is struck after a pound is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is an Australian form of address, like mate, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a mate or pal, also addressed as 'sport'.

clue.text: Fruit bats

explanation.definitionFit: The tropical fruit's plural is also slang for crazy, the same sense as bats.

clue.text: Kissed and cuddled, spoiling ace dress

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the letters are damaged and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple embrace and in doing so crumple a fine frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle someone affectionately is to touch them tenderly.

clue.text: Extend tax period

definitions.meaning: to extend is to lengthen or draw out
to tax is to strain or test to the limit
a period of time, especially a prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lengthen, to strain someone's resources, and a spell of time such as a prison term.

clue.text: Playwright introduced by top interviewer

indicators.note: the name is carried within the words top interviewer, which bring it in

explanation.surface: A dramatist is brought on by a leading interviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is spread across 'toP INTERviewer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold, author of The Caretaker and Betrayal, was a Nobel-winning dramatist.

clue.text: Mostly in bad taste, wearing one?

definitions.text: Mostly in bad taste, wearing one?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: manky is British slang for grotty or distasteful
if you are in a garment you are wearing it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Anyone wearing this is arguably in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts MANKY, British slang for grotty, to MANK. The whole clue describes the garment too.
explanation.definitionFit: The skimpy men's sling swimsuit is widely seen as tasteless, which the clue as a whole suggests.

clue.text: Shown in court, a nude picture

indicators.note: the words a nude are shown inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: A naked image is displayed in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' is a film: the 1972 musical with Liza Minnelli.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this is the title of a famous film musical.

clue.text: Moor that is covered in sheep

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is sits covered inside the word for sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Moorland, so to speak, is covered in sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' is the verb: to tie a boat up.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to make it fast, securing it with ropes.

clue.text: Person in commanding position takes flight once in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in disarray and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A commander flees once things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: From the children's game, the phrase describes whoever holds the top, dominant position.

clue.text: Daredevil caught fleeing collision

indicators.note: fleeing means the letter for caught leaves the word

parts.note: a crash is a collision
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A reckless driver is caught running from the scene of an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Here used as an adjective for reckless, as a daredevil is.

clue.text: Day finishes off with joint that's enjoyed by mates

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
ends means finishes off
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Friday finishes with a joint shared among friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Companionship is the bond that pals share.
